title: Health Claim Document Extraction
summary: Turn hospital bills, discharge summaries and investigation reports into structured, checked claim data, with uncertain fields routed to an assessor instead of guessed.

seo.title: Health Claim Document Extraction with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that reads hospital bills, discharge summaries and reports, extracts claim fields, runs policy checks and flags exceptions for assessors.

problem.intro: A single cashless or reimbursement claim can arrive as dozens of pages: scanned bills, pharmacy receipts, discharge summaries, lab reports and ID proofs, often photographed on a phone. Assessors re-type the same fields into the claims system before they can start the real work of adjudication.

pain_points.title: Manual data entry before any decision
pain_points.detail: Assessors spend their first pass keying patient, hospital, diagnosis, dates and line-item amounts instead of judging the claim.

pain_points.title: Inconsistent document quality
pain_points.detail: Skewed scans, handwritten notes and mixed languages make template-based OCR break on every new hospital format.

pain_points.title: Missed mismatches
pain_points.detail: Dates of admission, room category or billed procedures that contradict the discharge summary are easy to miss under volume.

pain_points.title: Turnaround pressure
pain_points.detail: Regulatory and customer expectations on claim turnaround leave little time for document chasing and rework.

solution.overview: We build a claim document pipeline that accepts the whole claim file, splits it into individual documents, classifies each one and extracts the fields your adjudication process needs. A large language model reads the documents in context, so a field that appears differently on two hospitals' bills is still captured. Every extracted value carries a confidence score and a link back to the page it came from. Low-confidence fields and rule failures go to an assessor queue, and clean claims move straight to the claims system with an audit trail.
capabilities: Splits and classifies mixed claim files: bills, discharge summaries, lab reports, prescriptions, KYC
Extracts header fields and bill line items, including handwritten and phone-photographed pages
Cross-checks dates, room category, diagnosis and procedures across documents
Applies configurable policy rules such as sub-limits, room-rent caps and waiting periods
Flags possible duplicates against previously submitted claims
Shows every value with its source page so assessors can verify in one click

workflow.title: Receive the claim file
workflow.detail: Documents arrive from the hospital portal, email or a TPA upload, and are grouped by claim number.

workflow.title: Split and classify
workflow.detail: Each page is assigned to a document type so the right extraction schema is applied.

workflow.title: Extract fields
workflow.detail: OCR plus an LLM extract structured fields and bill line items, each with a confidence score and page reference.

workflow.title: Check confidence
workflow.detail: Fields below the agreed threshold are sent to an assessor for confirmation instead of being guessed.

workflow.title: Run policy and consistency checks
workflow.detail: Rules compare documents with each other and with the policy schedule, and flag duplicates.

workflow.title: Hand over to the claims system
workflow.detail: Structured data, flags and the evidence trail are pushed to the core claims system for adjudication.

inputs: Hospital final bill and itemised bill
outputs: Structured claim record with header fields and line items
Field-level confidence scores with source-page links
List of policy and consistency flags
Audit trail of extraction and reviewer edits
human_in_the_loop: Assessors confirm any field below the confidence threshold and decide every flagged exception. The system never approves or rejects a claim; it prepares the file so the assessor starts with clean, verifiable data.
integrations: Core claims or TPA platform (via API or SFTP)
Email inboxes used for claim intake
guardrails: Confidence thresholds per field, agreed with the claims team
No auto-decision on claims; humans adjudicate
Personal and health data masked in logs and kept in your cloud region
Every value traceable to a source page
Regular sampling of auto-cleared claims for quality review
compliance_notes: Designed to support data minimisation and purpose limitation under India's DPDP Act 2023.
Keeps the audit trail insurers need to evidence how each claim was assessed under IRDAI expectations.

pilot.scope: One claim type (for example cashless hospitalisation) from two or three high-volume hospitals, run in parallel with your current process.

Working pipeline on a sample of real, de-identified claims
Field-level accuracy report against assessor-entered data
Production roll-out plan and cost estimate

faqs.q: Does this work on handwritten and phone-photographed documents?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. The pipeline handles skewed photos and common handwriting on bills and prescriptions, and any field it is unsure about is sent for human confirmation rather than guessed. The pilot report shows accuracy separately for printed and handwritten fields.

faqs.q: Will the AI approve or reject claims?
faqs.a: No. It prepares structured, checked data and flags issues. Adjudication stays with your assessors and medical team.

In your cloud account or an India region of a major cloud provider, depending on your policy. Health and personal data is masked in logs, and we can use models that do not retain or train on your data.

faqs.q: How does it connect to our claims system?
faqs.a: Through your system's API, an SFTP drop or a database staging table. We agree the format with your IT team during the pilot.
